after:
During the **working stroke** the spring-loaded drive pawl bears on a radial tooth face and pushes the wheel counter-clockwise. On the **return stroke** it slides up the sloped flank and clicks into the next space, while the **holding pawl** keeps the wheel from turning back. Clockwise rotation is blocked because a radial face meets each pawl tip.

*Idealization:* rigid, frictionless kinematics; spring forces, wear and load capacity are not modelled.
title: Ratchet and pawl · one-way advance
before: A **ratchet** converts an oscillating motion into intermittent rotation in one direction only. Here a crank on its own bearing post drives a coupler, which swings a lever about the wheel shaft by a bit more than one tooth pitch.
caption: A crank-rocker four-bar swings a lever about the ratchet shaft. The drive pawl on the lever pushes the wheel one tooth counter-clockwise in the working stroke; on the return the wheel stays still while the holding pawl, pinned to the base, blocks clockwise motion. Idealized rigid kinematics.
